learningObjectives: Model testable business criteria and basic grouping.
Calculate or manually enter risk weights without confusing class scales with output.
Link TestCases and associate ExecutionLists at their appropriate targets.
Distinguish linking, WorkState contribution, refreshed metrics and result aggregation.

elements.text: Functional criteria describe behavior, such as processing a payment; non-functional criteria describe quality, such as a measurable response-time target. Define testable acceptance criteria with stakeholders.

Folders organize RequirementSets; sets contain Requirements. Folders and Requirements may contain further structure, so this is a basic grouping example, not exactly three compulsory levels. TestCase links belong to the corresponding Requirement.

Associate relevant ExecutionLists with the RequirementSet, directly or through its ExecutionList configuration. An ExecutionEntry can also create a TestCase link on a Requirement; associated-list linking depends on AlwaysAdd, AskUser or NeverAdd configuration.
Requirements Management needs its AddIn enabled for editing and a valid license. Linking newly created objects in multi-user workspaces requires check-in. These are separate concerns from WorkState.

elements.text: New Requirements default to weight 1. Teams can enter weights manually, or calculate them with Damage class and Frequency class. The classes use a 0–10 scale; the resulting Weight is not restricted to 1–10.

With both classes, Weight = 2^Damage class × 2^Frequency class. For damage 3 and frequency 4, this yields 128. With one class, use its corresponding power of two. Higher weights increase relative contribution to risk-based metrics.

Relative Weight compares a weight with the total set weight. For parent Requirements, Aggregated Weight can instead sum directly subordinate weights. Weight is a business prioritization input, not evidence that tests passed.

elements.text: Create a TestCase Link placeholder or drop a TestCase directly onto its Requirement; one case can link to a given Requirement only once. COMPLETED is not required to create the link. It affects the coverage calculation: PLANNED contributes 20%, IN_WORK 50% and COMPLETED 100%.

For explicit execution grouping, create an ExecutionList configuration on the RequirementSet and drop the intended lists into it. Review which configurations are enabled. A link alone does not demonstrate that a compliance criterion passed.

AutoCalculateRequirements defaults to Off. For stale values, use Update Outdated Values on the RequirementSet. Automatic calculation can be enabled in Commander advanced settings and requires restart; assess repository wait times.

Coverage Specified, Coverage Executed and Execution State are distinct metrics. They consider weights and WorkState, rather than simply counting linked tests. Under default Result Aggregation First, use the first Passed/Failed result across associated lists, skipping No Result; Each considers all results. Neither means always use the newest run.

Independent inspection exercise: link an IN_WORK test and inspect its weighted coverage, associate an execution list, refresh values and examine its result. Then compare a COMPLETED state and deliberate aggregation setting. This documentation-based exercise was not executed in Tosca.

Cross-topic recap: default list insertion is once; repeat execution can be configured. TestStepLibraries hold reusable sequences in TestCases. TCP lookup uses {CP[Name]}. MONTHLAST selects month-end; include dd in a date format when the day needs to be visible. Date formatting and locale must be explicit when comparing output.

Original Academy videos, Knowledge Check and Exercise 22 were inaccessible. The local material is independent documentation-based practice; its scenarios do not certify the original exercise procedure or exam wording.

examPitfalls.title: Linking vs completion
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming a case must be COMPLETED to link.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: WorkState affects coverage contribution; check-in is required for newly created multi-user objects.

examPitfalls.title: Associated lists
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Dropping every list onto an atomic criterion.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Associate lists with the set or its configurations; ExecutionEntry linking can additionally create TestCase links.

examPitfalls.title: Basic grouping
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating the example hierarchy as exactly three compulsory levels.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Allow nested organization while preserving the set and criterion relationship.

examPitfalls.title: Recalculation
examPitfalls.bestPractice: AutoCalculateRequirements defaults Off; refresh stale values or configure automatic calculation deliberately.

examPitfalls.title: Quality criteria
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Confusing measured performance with payment behavior.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Define measurable acceptance criteria for both functional and non-functional requirements.

examPitfalls.title: Calculated output
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Confusing the 0–10 class scale with a Weight cap.

examPitfalls.title: Manual weights
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Manual weight entry is supported; use stakeholder risk priorities.

practiceQuiz.scenario: With default settings, how many times can the same TestCase be dragged onto the same ExecutionList before configuring multiple references?

options.text: Once by default; repeated execution requires deliberate repetition or multiple-reference setup.
The number is set in the TestCase properties tab

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish insertion defaults from configurable repetition.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Default insertion is once; supported repeat mechanisms do not imply unlimited default drag/drop.

optionExplanations.A: Correctly separates default insertion from repeat setup.
optionExplanations.B: Repetitions and multiple references are supported.
optionExplanations.C: A fixed two-entry allowance is not the documented default.
optionExplanations.D: The relevant setting is multiple-reference configuration, not this TestCase property.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Requirement uses both Damage class 3 and Frequency class 4. Which describes its calculated Weight in current Tosca?

options.text: It must stay within 1–10 because that is the class scale.
2^3 × 2^4 = 128; Weight can also be entered manually.
It is fixed by complexity and cannot be changed.

practiceQuiz.hint: The class scale and calculated output differ.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Two powers of two are multiplied. Manual assignment is an alternative; the output is not capped at 10.

optionExplanations.A: 0–10 applies to the input classes, not an output cap.
optionExplanations.B: Multiplying 8 by 16 yields 128, and manual entry is supported.
optionExplanations.C: Adding the classes is not the documented calculation.
optionExplanations.D: Teams can change weights to represent business risk.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where do you drop a TestCase to create traceability to a particular business criterion?

options.text: TestCases are not linked to the Requirement section

practiceQuiz.rationale: The corresponding Requirement receives its TestCase link. ExecutionList association is at set level.

optionExplanations.A: A folder provides organization, not this criterion-specific link.
optionExplanations.B: A set groups criteria and execution associations.
optionExplanations.C: The corresponding Requirement receives the TestCase link.
optionExplanations.D: TestCase links are supported in Requirements.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where is a TestStepLibrary containing Reusable TestStepBlocks used?
practiceQuiz.rationale: TestCase reuse uses TestStepLibraries and linked reusable sequences.

optionExplanations.A: Business criteria do not hold these reusable sequences.
optionExplanations.B: Technical models differ from reusable TestStepBlocks.
optionExplanations.C: Data-design objects differ from a TestStepLibrary.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which expression reads a Test Configuration Parameter named NameOfTheTCP in a TestStepValue?
practiceQuiz.hint: Outer curly braces, CP prefix, name in square brackets.
practiceQuiz.rationale: CP precedes square brackets containing the name; outer curly braces enclose the expression.

optionExplanations.A: This uses the documented CP expression delimiters.
optionExplanations.B: The brackets and braces are reversed.
optionExplanations.C: The outer braces required for an expression are missing.
optionExplanations.D: TCP is not the expression prefix; use CP.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Using a base date of 15 June 2025 and an English locale, which expression displays the last day of that month three years earlier as 30Jun2022?
practiceQuiz.hint: Include the day in the output to distinguish the last day from another day.
practiceQuiz.rationale: MONTHLAST applies the month-end operation and -3y shift; dd displays the day, MMM the abbreviated month and yyyy the four-digit year.

optionExplanations.A: MONTHFIRST selects the first day, so the output differs.
optionExplanations.B: The expression includes month-end, the negative year shift and a visible day.
optionExplanations.C: DATE retains the base day 15; it does not select month-end.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team wants risk-based reporting for a compliance criterion using an ExecutionList. Which setup provides the required associations?

options.text: Add the requirement text as a comment inside the ExecutionList.
Copy the Requirement into the ExecutionList description field.
Link the relevant TestCase to its Requirement and associate the ExecutionList with the containing RequirementSet.
ExecutionLists cannot be linked to Requirements in Tosca.

practiceQuiz.hint: Trace the criterion through its test and the associated run list.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Criterion-to-test and set-to-execution associations support reporting; comments alone do not establish those links or prove compliance.

optionExplanations.A: A comment does not create coverage or execution associations.
optionExplanations.B: Description text does not create the required links.
optionExplanations.C: These two associations connect the criterion, its test and the execution list.
optionExplanations.D: ExecutionLists can be associated with RequirementSets.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which order describes a basic grouping in the Requirements section, allowing additional nested folders or Requirements?
practiceQuiz.hint: A Folder groups Sets — so the Folder sits a level UP.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Folders group sets, which contain Requirements. This basic example is not a limit of exactly three levels.

optionExplanations.B: Folders group sets; this places the folder below its set.
optionExplanations.C: This moves the folder beneath its contained criteria.
optionExplanations.D: This is the basic grouping, with possible additional nesting.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where can a tester create an ExecutionList configuration that groups lists for a set of business criteria?

options.text: On the RequirementSet; then drop the lists into the configuration.
Onto each individual Requirement, one at a time.
Onto the RequirementFolder at the very top.
ExecutionLists cannot be linked to Requirements.

practiceQuiz.hint: The configuration belongs to the group of criteria.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Create ExecutionList Configuration on the RequirementSet, then add lists to that container.

optionExplanations.A: This is the documented configuration container and workflow.
optionExplanations.B: Individual criteria receive TestCase links, not this set-level configuration.
optionExplanations.C: The configuration is created on a RequirementSet.

practiceQuiz.scenario: AutoCalculateRequirements is Off. After links or test states change, displayed coverage is stale. What is the correct next step?

options.text: Right-click the RequirementSet and select 'Update Outdated Values'.
Re-run the entire ExecutionList from scratch.
Restart Tosca Commander to force a refresh.

practiceQuiz.hint: There is a dedicated right-click command to refresh values.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The dedicated recalculation command updates stale values. With automatic calculation enabled, manual refresh is not an unconditional requirement.

optionExplanations.A: Stale values alone do not warrant deleting valid links.
optionExplanations.B: This recalculates the stale metrics under the stated setting.
optionExplanations.C: Executing again does not replace required metric recalculation.
optionExplanations.D: A restart is needed for a setting change, not this manual refresh.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following is a NON-functional requirement for an online web shop?

options.text: The shop must be able to process credit card payments.
The shop must let users add items to a cart.
The shop must load any product page within 2 seconds (performance).
The shop must calculate shipping costs.

practiceQuiz.hint: Non-functional = a quality attribute, not a specific behavior.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Performance (page load within 2 seconds) is a non-functional requirement — it describes an operational quality attribute. Processing payments, adding to cart, and calculating shipping are functional requirements (specific behaviors the SUT must perform).

optionExplanations.C: A response-time limit is a measurable quality criterion.

quickRecap.value: Folders contain sets; sets contain criteria; nesting is possible.
Corresponding Requirement; completion affects metrics, not link eligibility.
Manual by default; AutoCalculateRequirements can update automatically.
Manual entry or 2^Damage × 2^Frequency; not capped at 10.
First qualifying result by default; Each considers all associated results.
